'''Daniel Carvajal Ramos''' ({{IPA|es|daˈnjel kaɾβaˈxal ˈramos}}; born 11 January 1992) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|right-back]] for [[La Liga]] club [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] and the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]]. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest right-backs of his generation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=19 May 2026 |title=Where Does Dani Carvajal Rank Among Real Madrid's All-Time Greats? |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/where-does-dani-carvajal-rank-real-madrid-all-time-greats |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=21 October 2025 |title=The 20 Best Right Backs in Soccer History––Ranked |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/the-best-right-backs-in-soccer-history-ranked |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=21 January 2025 |title=EA FC 25 TOTY: Van Dijk, Saliba, Carvajal and Grimaldo form dream defence |url=https://www.90min.com/ea-fc-25-toty-van-dijk-saliba-carvajal-and-grimaldo-dream-defence |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=90min.com |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mitton |first=Alex |date=27 August 2024 |title=Ranking the 9 Best Right-Backs in Champions League History |url=https://www.givemesport.com/champions-league-best-right-back-ever-ranked-cafu-lahm/ |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=GiveMeSport |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rodrigo and Carvajal, FIFPRO World 11 2024 {{!}} www.rfef.es/en |url=https://rfef.es/en/noticias/rodrigo-and-carvajal-fifpro-world-11-2024 |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=rfef.es |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Nwokolo |first=Collins |date=16 June 2024 |title=Top 10 Best Full-Backs In The World (2024) |url=https://topsoccerblog.com/top-best-full-backs-in-the-world/ |access-date=10 July 2026 |website=Top Soccer Blog |language=en-US}}</ref>

Having risen through the [[Real Madrid CF (youth)|Real Madrid youth]] ranks, Carvajal spent a season with [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] before returning to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]. He joined the first team in 2013 and has since won 27 major trophies at Real Madrid including four La Liga titles, two [[Copa del Rey]] titles and a joint record six [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] wins, a record he shares with [[Paco Gento]], [[Luka Modrić]], [[Toni Kroos]] and [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]].

At the youth international level, Carvajal won the [[2011 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|2011 European Championship]] with the [[Spain national under-19 football team|under-19 team]] and the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2013 edition]] with the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 team]]. He made his [[Spain national football team|senior]] debut in 2014, representing the nation at the [[FIFA World Cup]] in [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]] and [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]]. In [[UEFA Euro 2024|2024]], he was part of the [[UEFA Euro 2024 squads#Spain|Spain squad]] that won the [[UEFA European Championship]]. Carvajal also scored the decisive [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty]] at the [[2023 UEFA Nations League Finals]], securing Spain's first [[UEFA Nations League]] title.

==Club career==
===Real Madrid Castilla===
Carvajal was born in [[Leganés]], a suburb of [[Madrid]]. He joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s youth system as a 10-year-old, and continued climbing through the ranks until reaching [[Real Madrid Castilla]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/05/24/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1369401797.html|title=Dani Carvajal: "Nací siendo del Real Madrid"|trans-title=Dani Carvajal: "I was born a Real Madrid fan"|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=24 May 2013|access-date=24 October 2012}}</ref>

In [[2010–11 Segunda División B|his first season]] as a senior, Carvajal was immediately cast in the [[reserve team]]'s starting XI, also being the team's [[Captain (association football)|captain]]. In [[2011–12 Segunda División B|the following campaign]], he fared even better (38 games and two goals, [[2012 Segunda División B play-offs|playoffs]] included), as the Bs returned to [[Segunda División]] after a five-year absence.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2012/07/10/actualidad/1341929494_839108.html|title=Carvajal, el lateral que no pudo debutar con el Madrid|trans-title=Carvajal, the fullback who could not make Madrid debut|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=11 July 2012|access-date=24 October 2012}}</ref>

===Bayer Leverkusen===
On 11 July 2012, after failing to make a single appearance for Real's first team,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/liga-bbva/2012/07/06/la-marcha-de-carvajal-ratifica-la-poca-confianza-de-mourinho-en-la-cantera-blanca-101442/|title=La marcha de Carvajal ratifica la poca confianza de Mourinho en la cantera blanca|trans-title=Carvajal departure confirms Mourinho's little confidence in white youth system|newspaper=[[El Confidencial]]|language=es|date=6 July 2012|access-date=24 October 2012|archive-date=3 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903160613/http://www.elconfidencial.com/deportes/liga-bbva/2012/07/06/la-marcha-de-carvajal-ratifica-la-poca-confianza-de-mourinho-en-la-cantera-blanca-101442|url-status=dead}}</ref> Carvajal signed a five-year contract with Germany's [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] for a transfer fee of [[Euro|€]]5&nbsp;million. The Spaniards added on a buy-back clause in the region of €6.5&nbsp;million if they wanted to re-sign the player after one season, €7&nbsp;million after two and approximately €8.5&nbsp;million after three.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.abc.es/20120711/deportes-futbol/abci-bayer-carvajal-201207111155.html|title=El Bayer Leverkusen confirma el fichaje de Carvajal|trans-title=Bayer Leverkusen confirm signing of Carvajal|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|language=es|date=11 July 2012|access-date=24 October 2012 }}</ref>

Carvajal made his [[Bundesliga]] debut on 1 September 2012 in a 2–0 home win against [[SC Freiburg]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/346393/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Bayer Leverkusen 2–0 SC Freiburg|publisher=[[ESPN FC]]|date=1 September 2012|access-date=24 October 2012}}</ref> being subsequently named to the Team of the Week.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/bundesliga/elf-des-tages/2012-13/2|title=1. Bundesliga&nbsp;– Elf des Tages|trans-title=1. Bundesliga&nbsp;– Team of the Week|publisher=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|kicker]]|language=de|access-date=3 September 2012}}</ref> He scored his first goal for his new club on 25 November, netting the second in an eventual 2–1 success at [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|TSG Hoffenheim]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/346287/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=TSG Hoffenheim 1–2 Bayer Leverkusen|publisher=ESPN FC|date=25 November 2012|access-date=26 November 2012}}</ref>

Carvajal was selected as one of the three best right backs at the end of [[2012–13 Bundesliga|his first and only season]], behind [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]'s [[Phillip Lahm]] and [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]]'s [[Atsuto Uchida]]. He received 16% of the total vote from the fans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/fanzone/team-of-the-season/|title=Team of the season 2012/13|publisher=[[Bundesliga]]|date=25 May 2013|access-date=1 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140412230941/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/fanzone/team-of-the-season/|archive-date=12 April 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:Daniel Carvajal 2015.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Carvajal with [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2015]]
On 3 June 2013, Real Madrid exercised their buy-back option on Carvajal, who became the team's first signing for [[2013–14 La Liga|2013–14]] for a fee believed to be in the region of €6.5&nbsp;million. This was confirmed by Bayer's [[director of football]] [[Rudi Völler]], who stated: "Real Madrid noticed the outstanding performances by Dani this season, and it was only a matter of time before they exercised their buy-back option."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bayer04.de/B04-ENG/en/_site_index.aspx|title=Real Madrid recall Carvajal|publisher=Bayer Leverkusen|date=3 June 2013|access-date=3 June 2013}}</ref> Shortly after the move, he spoke of his happiness to return, thanking the president, the fans and the club at a press conference.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2892/transfer-zone/2013/07/05/4096427/carvajal-revels-in-real-madrid-return?ICID=OP|title=Carvajal revels in Real Madrid return|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=5 July 2013|access-date=13 July 2013}}</ref>

Carvajal made his [[La Liga]] debut on 18 August 2013, in a 2–1 home win against [[Real Betis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/373215/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Isco an instant hero|publisher=ESPN FC|date=18 August 2013|access-date=29 November 2013}}</ref> One month later he played his first match in the [[UEFA Champions League]], again featuring the full 90 minutes in a 6–1 away victory of [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] in [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|the group stage]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011769--galatasaray-vs-real-madrid/|title=Six-goal Madrid overwhelm Galatasaray|publisher=UEFA|date=17 September 2013|access-date=29 November 2013}}</ref>

Carvajal appeared in 45 matches in [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|his first season]] and scored twice, in the league against [[Rayo Vallecano]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/primera/jornada_31/rma_ray/|title=Goles para aguantar el chaparrón|trans-title=Goals to stem storm|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=29 March 2014|access-date=2 June 2014}}</ref> and [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/primera/jornada_35/rma_osa/|title=Calma antes de la tempestad|trans-title=Calm before the storm|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=26 April 2014|access-date=2 June 2014}}</ref> He added 120 minutes in [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|the Champions League final]], a 4–1 triumph over [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Atlético Madrid|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=24 May 2014|access-date=25 May 2014}}</ref>

Carvajal started in Real Madrid's triumphs in the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup]] over compatriots [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]],<!--rem deprecated source (dailymail)--> and in [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup|that year]]'s [[FIFA Club World Cup]] [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]] against Argentina's [[San Lorenzo de Almagro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=259701/match=300298898/match-report.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141220234228/http://www.fifa.com/clubworldcup/matches/round=259701/match=300298898/match-report.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 December 2014|title=Real Madrid coast to Morocco 2014 title|publisher=FIFA|date=20 December 2014|access-date=6 May 2015}}</ref> In the first leg of [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|the Champions League's semi-finals]], on 5 May 2015, he conceded a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] by fouling [[Carlos Tevez]], with the [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] forward converting the spot-kick to defeat the Spaniards 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32582191|title=Juventus 2–1 Real Madrid|work=BBC Sport|last1=Henson|first1=Mike|date=5 May 2015|access-date=6 May 2015}}</ref>

On 8 July 2015, Carvajal signed a new deal with the ''Merengues'' until 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/carvajal-at-real-madrid-until-2020|title=Carvajal at Real Madrid until 2020|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=8 July 2014|access-date=8 July 2014}}</ref> He contributed with eight appearances and one goal against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2015738--shakhtar-vs-real-madrid/|title=Ronaldo-inspired Madrid hold off Shakhtar|publisher=UEFA|date=25 November 2015|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref> in [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|the campaign's Champions League]], as the tournament ended in win; in [[2016 UEFA Champions League Final|the final]] against Atlético Madrid, he was subbed off injured early into the second half of a 1–1 draw ([[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] triumph).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|publisher=UEFA|date=28 May 2016|access-date=29 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/champions/carvajal-lesion-lagrimas-5165730|title=Carvajal: Lesión y lágrimas|trans-title=Carvajal: Injury and tears|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|language=es|date=28 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref>

On 9 August 2016, Carvajal started in the [[UEFA Super Cup]] clash against Sevilla in [[Trondheim]], and scored the final [[2016 UEFA Super Cup|3–2]] in the 119th minute after an individual effort.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.co.uk/report?gameId=450351|title=Dani Carvajal's late goal in ET helps Real Madrid win UEFA Super Cup|publisher=ESPN FC|date=9 August 2016|access-date=9 August 2016}}</ref> During [[2016–17 La Liga|the league season]], in spite of several physical ailments,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2017/01/18/primera/1484769997_620497.html|title=Carvajal, tres o cuatro semanas de baja por una lesión muscular|trans-title=Carvajal, three to four weeks out due to muscle injury|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|date=18 January 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2017/01/21/actualidad/1485022287_929107.html|title=Ni las lesiones dan minutos a Danilo|trans-title=Not even injuries give minutes to Danilo|newspaper=El País|date=21 January 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2017/05/03/actualidad/1493815809_710980.html|title=Carvajal sufre una rotura y se pierde lo que resta de Liga|trans-title=Carvajal ruptures himself and loses rest of League|newspaper=El País|date=3 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> he still contributed with 23 games to help the team be crowned champions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|trans-title=Real Madrid, LaLiga Santander champions 2016/17|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Malaga 0–2 Real Madrid|work=BBC Sport|date=21 May 2017|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> On 3 December 2016, after [[Sergio Ramos]] had equalised in the last minute against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] at the [[Camp Nou]], he [[Goal celebration|celebrated the goal]] by giving opposing fans the middle finger,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2017/04/24/58fe5ed8ca47413f548b461c.html|title=Real Madrid-Barcelona: Celebrations in enemy territory|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|date=24 April 2017|access-date=16 October 2018}}</ref> but later apologised;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/dani-carvajal-middle-finger-barcelona-fans-el-clasico-sergio-ramos-goal-120316|title=Dani Carvajal apologizes for flipping the bird to Barcelona fans after Ramos goal|work=[[Fox Sports]]|last=Dowd|first=Phil|date=9 December 2016|access-date=16 October 2018}}</ref> after nearly one month on the sidelines, he returned to action just in time to start at the [[2017 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]] on 3 June, which they won for the third time in four years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|publisher=UEFA|date=3 June 2017|access-date=4 June 2017}}</ref>

[[File:Ofrenda de la Liga y la Champions-10-L.Millán (52109524294).jpg|thumb|Carvajal in a trophy presentation ceremony at [[Virgin of Almudena]] in 2022]]
On 17 September 2017, Carvajal's contract was extended until 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/ceremony-to-mark-carvajals-contract-renewal|title=Ceremony to mark Carvajal's contract renewal|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=17 September 2017|access-date=18 September 2017}}</ref> Early in the following month, he was sidelined with a heart condition;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/real-madrid/story/3218312/real-madrid-defender-dani-carvajal-ruled-out-with-heart-problem|title=Real Madrid defender Dani Carvajal ruled out with heart problem|publisher=ESPN FC|date=2 October 2017|access-date=6 October 2017}}</ref> he made eight appearances during [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|that year's Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcnradio.com/deportes/asi-llegan-las-plantillas-de-real-madrid-y-liverpool-la-final-de-la-champions|title=Así llegan Real Madrid y Liverpool a la final de la Champions|trans-title=That is how Real Madrid and Liverpool arrive to the Champions final|publisher=[[RCN Radio]]|language=es|date=25 May 2018|access-date=29 May 2018}}</ref> and Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall title in the competition. In [[2018 UEFA Champions League final|the decisive match]] against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] he was forced to leave the pitch due to an injury, in an eventual 3–1 win at the [[Olympic Stadium (Kyiv)|Olympic Stadium]] in Kyiv.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/|title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick|publisher=UEFA|date=26 May 2018|access-date=28 May 2018}}</ref>

Carvajal scored Real Madrid's first league goal of [[2018–19 Real Madrid CF season|the new season]] on 19 August 2018, in a 2–0 home victory over [[Getafe CF|Getafe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45242415|title=Real Madrid 2–0 Getafe|work=BBC Sport|date=19 August 2018|access-date=31 December 2018}}</ref>

The next season, Carvajal was a regular starter as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]].<ref name=Liga>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|website=Marca|location=Spain}}</ref> On 29 July 2021, he extended his contract until June 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Official Announcement: Dani Carvajal|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/07/29/official-announcement-dani-carvajal|access-date=29 July 2021|website=Real Madrid C.F. – Web Oficial}}</ref>

On 1 June 2024, he scored his second Champions League goal from a header in a 2–0 victory over [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the [[2024 UEFA Champions League final|final]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Peter |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/b-dortmund-vs-r-madrid/report/504385 |title=Borussia Dortmund 0–2 Real Madrid: Dani Carvajal and Vinicius Jr score as Los Blancos win 15th Champions League title |publisher=Sky Sports |date=1 June 2024 }}</ref> He also became the first player to win six finals in the competition along with [[Luka Modrić]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0252-0e98c715bb79-dea77f56e2bd-1000--champions-league-final-records-and-statistics/ |title=Champions League final records and statistics |publisher=UEFA |date=1 June 2024 }}</ref>

During the [[2024–25 Real Madrid CF season|2024–25 season]], with the departure of [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho]], Carvajal was promoted as vice-captain of the team. On 5 October 2024, Carvajal suffered a [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn Anterior cruciate ligament]] (ACL) along with lateral collateral ligament (LCL) and posterolateral corner injuries to his right knee during Real's match against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], he was ruled out for the rest of the [[2024–25 Real Madrid CF season|season]], with a recovery period estimated to be eight to ten months.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 October 2024 |title=Carvajal medical report |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/medical-reports/parte-medico-de-carvajal-06-10-2024 |access-date=6 October 2024 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanderson |first=Tom |date=6 October 2024 |title=Real Madrid Confirms Huge Double Injury Blow, With One Star Out For Rest Of Season |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomsanderson/2024/10/06/real-madrid-confirms-huge-double-injury-blow-with-one-star-out-for-rest-of-season/ |access-date=6 October 2024 |work=[[Forbes]] |language=en}}</ref> A day after the injury, his contract was extended until 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Official Announcement: Dani Carvajal signs contract renewal|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/latest-news/c-06-10-2024|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=6 October 2024|access-date=6 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 October 2024 |title=Dani Carvajal renews Real Madrid contract after suffering long-term knee injury |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5821957/2024/10/06/dani-carvajal-real-madrid-contract/ |access-date=6 October 2024 |publisher=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref>

On 9 July 2025, Carvajal made his return to action, coming on as a substitute against [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the semi-final of the [[2025 FIFA Club World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/el-regreso-de-carvajal-09-07-2025 |title=Carvajal returns to action |publisher=Real Madrid CF |date=9 July 2025 }}</ref> During the [[2025–26 Real Madrid CF season|2025–26 season]], Carvajal became captain of the team following the departure of [[Luka Modrić]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/la-liga/articles/real-madrid-reveal-new-captains-after-modric-and-lucas-vazquez-departures-2025-07-20 |title=Real Madrid Reveal New Captains After Modric and Lucas Vazquez Departures |publisher=beIN SPORTS |date=20 July 2025 }}</ref>

On 18 May 2026, Carvajal announced that he would leave Real Madrid at the end of the 2025–26 season, after 13 years and more than 400 matches in the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-carvajal-18-05-2026|title=Official Announcement: Carvajal |publisher=Real Madrid CF |date=18 May 2026 }}</ref>

=== Getafe ===
On 13 October 2026, Carvajal signed for La Liga club Getafe on a contract until 30 June 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 October 2026 |title=Daniel Carvajal, new player of Getafe CF |url=https://www.getafecf.com/en/news/daniel-carvajal-new-player-of-getafe-cf |access-date=13 October 2026 |publisher=[[Getafe CF]] |language=en}}</ref> 

==International career==
===Youth===
[[File:Dani Carvajal Spain u-19 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Carvajal with [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain under-19]] in 2010]]
Carvajal acted as backup to [[FC Barcelona]]'s [[Martín Montoya]] at the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]], playing in the 3–0 group stage win against [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|the Netherlands]] as [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain]] went on to win the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0decb84da2f4-4c763a4c7387-1000--spain-beat-netherlands-to-top-group-b/|title=Spain beat Netherlands to top Group B|publisher=UEFA|date=12 June 2013|access-date=2 June 2014}}</ref> He was selected by [[Spain national football team|full side]] manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] for his 30-man provisional squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]], being excused alongside all other Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid players from the warm-up game against [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]] on 30 May due to the Champions League final,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=5/news=del-bosque-waits-to-name-23-2343915.html|title=Del Bosque waits to name 23|publisher=FIFA|date=25 May 2014|access-date=2 June 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140528001519/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y%3D2014/m%3D5/news%3Ddel-bosque-waits-to-name-23-2343915.html|archive-date=28 May 2014}}</ref> and being omitted from the final list the following day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27647635|title=World Cup 2014: Spain drop Alvaro Negredo and Jesus Navas|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=31 May 2014|access-date=31 May 2014}}</ref>

===Senior===
On 29 August 2014, Carvajal received his first call-up to the [[Spain national football team|Spanish senior squad]] for friendly matches against [[France national football team|France]] and [[North Macedonia national football team|Macedonia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/these-are-players-called-matches-against-france-and-macedonia|title=Vicente del Bosque has announced the 23-man squad for the matches against France (September 4th) and Macedonia (September 8th)|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|date=29 August 2014|access-date=29 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831194953/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/these-are-players-called-matches-against-france-and-macedonia|archive-date=31 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He debuted on 4 September in a 0–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] loss to the former in which he played the full 90 minutes.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Dani Carvajal debutó con la Selección absoluta|url=https://www.defensacentral.com/real_madrid/110908-dani-carvajal-debuto-con-la-seleccion-absoluta|website=Defensa Central|date=5 September 2014|access-date=19 August 2024|language=es}}</ref> In May 2016, Carvajal was selected in the Spain squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36312769|title=Euro 2016: Diego Costa, Juan Mata & Fernando Torres not in Spain squad|work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2016|access-date=17 May 2016}}</ref> However, on 30 May, he withdrew from the squad with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2016/05/30/actualidad/1464604756_004662.html|title=Dani Carvajal se pierde la Eurocopa 2016|trans-title=Dani Carvajal misses 2016 European Championship|newspaper=El País|language=es|date=30 May 2016|access-date=30 May 2016}}</ref>

Carvajal was named in Spain's final [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|website=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|publisher=Platform Group|date=21 May 2018|access-date=21 May 2018}}</ref> After sitting out the first game against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] as he was not fully fit,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/06/15/portugal-vs-spain-world-cup-2018-live-score-latest-updates/|title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores sensational hat-trick as Portugal hold Spain in instant World Cup classic|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|date=15 June 2018|access-date=20 June 2018}}</ref> he made his first appearance in [[FIFA World Cup|the competition]] on 20 June and played the entire 1–0 win over [[Iran national football team|Iran]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2018/06/20/sports/soccer/ap-soc-wcup-iran-spain.html|title=Diego Costa scores again, Spain beats Iran 1–0 at World Cup|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=20 June 2018|access-date=20 June 2018}}</ref> He retained his place in the starting line-up for the final [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group B|Group B]] fixture against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]], assisting [[Iago Aspas]]' stoppage time equaliser in the 2–2 draw.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12098/11416733/spain-2-2-morocco-spain-top-group-b-after-dramatic-turnaround|title=Spain 2–2 Morocco: Spain top Group B after dramatic turnaround|website=[[Sky Sports]]|access-date=19 June 2024}}</ref> In the [[2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 16|round of 16]] loss to [[Russia national football team|Russia]], Carvajal appeared as a 70th-minute substitute for [[Nacho (footballer, born 1990)|Nacho Fernández]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-mena/articles-video/2018-fifa-world-cup-spain-1-russia-1-russia-w|title=2018 FIFA World Cup: Spain 1–1 Russia (Russia win on penalties)|website=[[BeIN Sports]]|access-date=19 June 2024}}</ref>
[[File:Iran vs Spain 2018 World Cup 16.jpg|thumb|Carvajal (white) with Spain at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]]]]
He once again missed out on the European Championships three years later, with manager [[Luis Enrique]] leaving him out of the Spain's [[UEFA Euro 2020]] squad due to injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carvajal becomes the first Real Madrid player to make Luis Enrique's Spain squad in 235 days |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2021/11/05/61851dc4268e3ec7658b45b4.html|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=5 November 2021|access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref> Spain went on to reach the semi-finals of the tournament, losing out to eventual champions [[Italy national football team|Italy]] on penalties.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/026b-12b19306ec6a-4aaeee9fb2ca-1000--italy-reach-final-on-penalties/ |title=Italy 1–1 Spain (pens: 4–2): Azzurri hold nerve to reach EURO final|website=[[UEFA]]|date=6 July 2021 |access-date=7 July 2021}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

Carvajal was included in Spain's squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar,<ref>{{cite news |title=Spain World Cup 2022 squad |url=https://www.reuters.com/graphics/WORLD-CUP/akveqzmgwvr/teams/spain/|website=[[Reuters]]|access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref> playing the full match against [[Germany national football team|Germany]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/nov/27/spain-germany-world-cup-group-e-match-report|first=Sid|last=Lowe|title=Spain 1–1 Germany: World Cup Group E – match report|website=The Guardian|date=27 November 2022 |access-date=19 June 2024}}</ref> and the second half against [[Japan national football team|Japan]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/dec/01/japan-spain-world-cup-group-e-match-report|first=Paul|last=McInnes|title=Japan 2–1 Spain: World Cup Group E – match report|website=The Guardian|date=December 2022 |access-date=19 June 2024}}</ref> during the [[2022 FIFA World Cup Group E|group stage]], as the team was again knocked out at the [[2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 16|round of 16]] in a penalty shootout against Morocco.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/articles/world-cup-qatar-2022-morocco-spain-match-review|title=World Cup Qatar 2022: Morocco vs. Spain {{!}} Match Review|website=FIFA|access-date=19 June 2024}}</ref>

Carvajal played for Spain in the [[2023 UEFA Nations League Finals]], scoring the winning penalty via [[Panenka (penalty kick)|panenka]] in the [[2023 UEFA Nations League final|final]] shoot-out against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]], following a goalless draw.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Spain win Nations League final on penalties|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65944659|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|access-date=21 June 2023}}</ref>

In 2024, he was named to the squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2024]].<ref>{{cite news |date=7 June 2024 |title=Official {{!}} Final Spain squad for the Euro 2024 finals |url=https://rfef.es/en/noticias/final-spain-squad-for-the-euro-2024-finals |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] |access-date=7 June 2024 }}</ref> On 15 June 2024, Carvajal scored his first international goal against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] in a 3–0 win in Spain's opening match at the European Championships.<ref>{{cite news |date=15 June 2024 |title=Dani Carvajal scores on Euro debut to make it Spain 3–0 Croatia|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/video-dani-carvajal-scores-euro-171100490.html|website=Yahoo! Sports|publisher=Yahoo!|access-date=15 June 2024 }}</ref> At the age of 32 years and 156 days, he became the oldest player to score for [[Spain at the UEFA European Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/football/story/_/id/40357033/euro-2024-stats-yamal-youngest-carvajal-oldest-albania-fastest|title=Euro 2024 stats: Yamal youngest, Carvajal oldest, Albania fastest|website=ESPN|date=16 June 2024 |access-date=19 June 2024}}</ref> In the quarter-finals against hosts [[Germany national football team|Germany]], he was sent-off for a double booking late into extra-time for preventing a counter-attack, ruling him out of the next match; Spain won 2–1 to go through to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/703939 |title=Spain 2–1 Germany (Jul 5, 2024) Game Analysis|website=[[ESPN]]|date=5 July 2024 |access-date=7 July 2024 }}</ref> He later featured in the 2–1 victory over [[England national football team|England]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2024 Final|final]], achieving the tournament's title with his country.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/realmadrid-2024-07-14-dani-carvajal-leads-spain-to-euro-2024-title-bellingham-goes-down-despite-brilliant-perfo/ |title=Dani Carvajal leads Spain to Euro 2024 title, Bellingham goes down despite brilliant performance|website=Tribuna|date=14 July 2024 }}</ref>

Carvajal was omitted from Spain's squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] by manager [[Luis de la Fuente (footballer, born 1961)|Luis de la Fuente]] due to injury struggles and lack of game time throughout the 2025–26 season, which affected his form.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kirkland |first1=Alex |title=Spain World Cup 2026 squad confirmed: Lamine Yamal stars, no Real Madrid players |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48870392/spain-world-cup-2026-squad-confirmed-lamine-yamal-stars-no-real-madrid-players |publisher=www.espn.com |access-date=13 July 2026 |date=25 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Madrid captain Carvajal in race against time for Spain's World Cup squad |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/5/7/madrid-captain-carvajal-in-race-against-time-for-spains-world-cup-squad |access-date=13 July 2026 |work=Al Jazeera |date=7 May 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Carvajal is known for his consistency, aggressive style, and his ability to assist his team both in defence and attack.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nesci |first1=Gianluca |title=4 unheralded players who will play crucial roles in the semi-finals |url=https://www.thescore.com/chlg/news/1288991 |publisher=theScore.com |access-date=3 June 2024 |language=en |date=2 May 2017}}</ref><ref name="serial winner">{{cite web |title=Dani Carvajal: Real Madrid's Model of Consistency Who Owes Much to Bayer Leverkusen |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/dani-carvajal-real-madrid-serial-winner-opinion |publisher=90min.com |access-date=3 June 2024 |date=13 August 2020}}</ref> A tenacious and tactically intelligent player, defensively he is known for his positioning, mentality, tackling, anticipation, and ability to intercept loose balls.<ref name="serial winner"/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Dorrington |first1=Nick |title=Marcelo and Dani Carvajal Provide Platform for Real Madrid Win over Barcelona |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2244346-marcelo-and-dani-carvajal-provide-platform-for-real-madrid-win-over-barcelona |publisher=Bleacher Report |access-date=3 June 2024 |language=en |date=25 October 2014}}</ref><ref name="Hard Work">{{cite web |last1=Dorrington |first1=Nick |title=Hard Work Has Earned Dani Carvajal His Place in Real Madrid's Team of Stars |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2398275-hard-work-has-earned-dani-carvajal-his-place-in-real-madrids-team-of-stars |publisher=Bleacher Report |access-date=3 June 2024 |language=en |date=17 March 2015}}</ref><ref name="Leganes boy">{{cite news |last1=McTear |first1=Adapted by Euan |title=Carvajal: The Leganes boy who made it at Real Madrid |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2017/04/03/58e2470ae5fdea50158b45d8.html |access-date=3 June 2024 |work=MARCA in English |date=3 April 2017 |language=en}}</ref> Going forward, he also possesses excellent technical skills and [[Cross (association football)|crossing]], as well as an ability to get forward with his overlapping runs due to this awareness.<ref name="serial winner"/><ref name="interview">{{cite web |title=Daniel Carvajal interview |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/0000239427.jsp |publisher=bundesliga.com |access-date=3 June 2024 |language=en |archive-date=3 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240603194245/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/0000239427.jsp |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Real Madrid's Dani Carvajal: Two crosses in 5–2 win |url=https://www.thescore.com/news/1484298 |publisher=theScore.com |access-date=3 June 2024 |language=en |date=11 February 2018}}</ref><ref name="extension">{{cite web |last1=Jones |first1=Matt |title=Dani Carvajal, Real Madrid Agree Contract Extension Until 2022 |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2710565-dani-carvajal-real-madrid-agree-contract-extension-until-2022 |publisher=Bleacher Report |access-date=3 June 2024 |language=en |date=18 September 2017}}</ref> In terms of his physical qualities, he also stands out for his speed, energy, and work-rate, despite his diminutive stature.<ref name="serial winner"/><ref name="Hard Work"/><ref name="Leganes boy"/><ref name="extension"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Real Madrid's UCL hero Dani Carvajal eyes passing legendary Paco Gento: 'Why not dream of getting another?' |url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/real-madrids-ucl-hero-dani-carvajal-eyes-passing-legendary-paco-gento-why-not-dream-of-getting-another/ |publisher=CBSSports.com |access-date=3 June 2024 |language=en |date=2 June 2024}}</ref> He is also highly regarded for his leadership qualities.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Corrigan |first1=Dermot |title=Dani Carvajal – Real Madrid's unlikely Champions League hero who laid foundations with Di Stefano |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5531578/2024/06/02/dani-carvajal-champions-league-di-stefano/ |access-date=4 June 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=2 June 2024}}</ref> Despite his ability, he has often struggled with injuries throughout his career.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rai |first1=Guillermo |title=Carvajal: Real Madrid's quiet 'animal' who refuses to go away despite injuries |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4247897/2023/02/24/real-madrids-dani-carvajal-the-quiet-animal-who-refuses-to-go-away-despite-injuries/ |access-date=3 June 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=24 February 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Carvajal's injury nightmare continues |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/09/19/6147971022601d6d518b4613.html |access-date=3 June 2024 |work=MARCA |date=19 September 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Brazilian former right-back [[Cafu]] described Carvajal as one of the best right-backs in the world in 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=LaLiga - Real Madrid: Cafu: It's been a long time since Real Madrid had a full-back like Carvajal |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2018/02/26/5a942a2122601de6458b4593.html |access-date=15 April 2026 |work=MARCA in English |date=26 February 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Carvajal is married to Daphne Cañizares, with whom he has a child. His wife's twin sister Melanie is married to Carvajal's former Madrid teammate [[Joselu]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Benito |first1=Alexandra |url=https://www.vanitatis.elconfidencial.com/famosos/2024-05-09/dapnhe-melanie-canizares-joselu-dani-carvajal_3669851/ |title=¿Quién es quién y cómo han cambiado? Las gemelas Daphne y Melanie Cañizares, mujeres de los futbolistas Joselu y Carvajal |publisher=Vanitatis |language=es |date=9 May 2024 }}</ref> His father is an inspector in the [[National Police Corps (Spain)|National Police]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2024/06/02/watch-dani-carvajal-father-real-madrid-bus-parade |title=(WATCH) Dani Carvajal's father leads Real Madrid bus on parade route |publisher=Football España |date=2 June 2024 }}</ref>

On 8 April 2026, Carvajal was put under investigation by a judge in Andorra for allegations of illegal watch smuggling.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/2026-04-08-dani-carvajal-among-several-footballers-charged-by-a-judge-for-buying-smuggled-luxury-wat/|title=Dani Carvajal among several footballers charged by a judge for buying smuggled luxury watches – reports|date=8 April 2026|accessdate=8 April 2026|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/futbol/20260408/11508732/juez-andorra-imputa-carvajal-otros-seis-futbolistas-comprar-relojes-lujo-contrabando.html|title=Un juez de Andorra imputa a Carvajal y otros seis futbolistas por comprar relojes de lujo de contrabando|date=8 April 2026|accessdate=8 April 2026|language=es}}</ref>
